conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable state controls whether PWM generation runs and whether the clock generator is requested. The state is written through the channel configuration path and is exposed by configuration read-back and the aggregate clock-enable output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The channel configuration write can modify cfg_en (lines 183-184), threatening the enable state's integrity. Clearing cfg_en resets the counters and disables channel operation (lines 212-225), and cfg_en drives the clock-enable outputs (lines 197 and 121), so it can block PWM operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite a channel's enable bit to disable PWM generation or enable an unintended channel.

conceptual assets.information: The prescaler and clock-divider settings select and divide the clock-generator tick used to advance each channel's PWM timing. PWM behavior depends on this configured timebase.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write changes cfg_prsc and cfg_cdiv (lines 183 and 185-187), so unauthorized modification can change the PWM timebase. The selected clkgen_i bit and divider comparison control whether and when timing advances (lines 214-220), so a bad setting can delay or withhold PWM updates.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a prescaler or divider value that selects an inactive tick source or makes PWM timing incorrect or effectively stalled.

conceptual assets.information: The duty-cycle setting determines how long each PWM cycle presents its active level. Each channel's configured duty value is used when generating the external PWM waveform and is available through read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A channel write changes cfg_duty (lines 183 and 188), and cfg_duty participates in the PWM level decision (line 231), so unauthorized modification can produce an incorrect duty cycle.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite the duty value so an external load receives an unintended PWM duty cycle.

conceptual assets.information: The polarity setting determines which logic level is active for each channel's PWM output. It is stored as part of the channel configuration and returned by configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A channel configuration write changes cfg_pol (lines 183 and 186), and cfg_pol selects the output level in both PWM branches (lines 231-234), so unauthorized modification can invert the externally consumed waveform.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change the polarity bit and invert a channel's control waveform.

conceptual assets.information: The decoded bus address selects which PWM channel receives a read or configuration write. This internal selection determines which repeated channel instance an access reaches and has no separate output representation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address comparison creates the per-channel selection that controls we and re (lines 109-111), so corruption can direct an access to the wrong channel and compromise configuration integrity. If no channel is selected, the access strobes are not generated, so a required configuration transfer can be withheld (lines 109-111).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could spoof or corrupt the bus address so a write changes the wrong channel or no channel accepts the requested access.

conceptual assets.information: The PWM waveform is the externally consumed timing and level behavior produced on pwm_o for the configured channels. External operation depends on its duty, polarity, enable, and timing behavior.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The channel logic assigns pwm_o from cfg_pol, cfg_duty, cfg_en, and cnt_duty (lines 231-234), so modification of those values or the output-producing logic can make the waveform incorrect. Disabling cfg_en resets the timing state and prevents normal PWM activity (lines 212-225), so the waveform can be blocked.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter channel configuration or PWM state so the external load receives an incorrect waveform or no PWM activity.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel duty-cycle phase count tracks the current position used to compare against the configured duty value. It is generated and held internally and is not carried whole through a unit port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: cnt_duty is stored and incremented internally (lines 206, 225, and 227) and directly determines the PWM level decision (line 231), so unauthorized modification can corrupt the waveform's duty behavior. A stuck or corrupted phase state can prevent the expected PWM transitions and block normal waveform operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the internal duty-phase count so a channel remains at an incorrect level or stops making the expected PWM transitions.
